note: Original concept records for the 40 pre-generator detection rules. Ids are fixed above the existing record range so generator allocation stays stable; text is DROBON-authored from each rule documented mechanism.

DPK-DAST-001.title: Concept: Cleartext HTTP transport
DPK-DAST-001.description: A response delivered over http:// crosses the network unencrypted, so any intermediary can read or rewrite it. The check reads only the observed URL scheme, which is why an HTTPS endpoint with a broken certificate is a different finding.
DPK-DAST-001.applicability: Public HTTP responses observed by the passive URL check; TLS configuration itself is not inspected.
DPK-DAST-001.risk: Content interception or modification on the path; MEDIUM.

DPK-DAST-002.title: Concept: Missing Content-Security-Policy
DPK-DAST-002.description: With no Content-Security-Policy the browser receives no restriction on where scripts, styles or frames may load from, so an injected element runs with the page default policy. The observation is header absence, not proof of an exploitable injection point.
DPK-DAST-002.applicability: HTML responses that omit the header; policies delivered only by meta tag are not seen by this check.
DPK-DAST-002.risk: Amplifies any cross-site scripting that reaches the page; MEDIUM.

DPK-DAST-003.title: Concept: HSTS without max-age
DPK-DAST-003.description: Strict-Transport-Security only instructs browsers for the number of seconds in max-age, and a directive without it is ignored. The signal is a policy that exists syntactically but cannot protect a session.
DPK-DAST-003.applicability: Responses that send Strict-Transport-Security and omit or zero max-age.
DPK-DAST-003.risk: Downgrade and cookie-hijack window stays open; MEDIUM.

DPK-DAST-004.title: Concept: Cookie without the Secure attribute
DPK-DAST-004.description: A cookie lacking Secure may be attached to a plaintext request, exposing its value to anyone on the path. The check inspects Set-Cookie attributes only; it does not judge whether the cookie is sensitive.
DPK-DAST-004.risk: Session token disclosure over HTTP; LOW per rule severity, higher where a session rides on it.

DPK-DAST-005.title: Concept: MIME sniffing left enabled
DPK-DAST-005.description: Without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff a browser may reinterpret a response as a different content type, turning an innocuous upload into script. The observation is a missing header, not a crafted file.
DPK-DAST-005.applicability: Responses that omit the nosniff directive.
DPK-DAST-005.risk: Content-type confusion enabling script execution; MEDIUM.

DPK-DAST-006.title: Concept: Cookie readable by script (no HttpOnly)
DPK-DAST-006.description: A cookie without HttpOnly is visible to document.cookie, so any script that runs on the origin can copy it. This check reports the attribute gap; it does not prove that a script-injection flaw exists.
DPK-DAST-006.risk: Session theft through any script-execution bug; LOW per rule severity.

DPK-DAST-007.title: Concept: Framing not restricted
DPK-DAST-007.description: Without X-Frame-Options or an equivalent frame-ancestors directive the page can be embedded by another origin and used as a clickjacking surface. Framing protection is a policy statement, not a runtime guarantee.
DPK-DAST-007.applicability: HTML responses that omit both framing headers; CSP frame-ancestors is evaluated in a separate check.
DPK-DAST-007.risk: Interface redressing and unintended user actions; MEDIUM.

DPK-DAST-008.title: Concept: Cookie without SameSite
DPK-DAST-008.description: A cookie without SameSite may be sent on cross-site navigations, which is the ingredient state-changing requests need for CSRF. Modern browsers default some cookies to Lax, so absence is a portability and intent gap as much as an exposure.
DPK-DAST-008.risk: Cross-site request forgery where other controls are absent; LOW.

DPK-DAST-009.title: Concept: Missing Referrer-Policy
DPK-DAST-009.description: Without Referrer-Policy the browser applies its default referrer behaviour, which can leak full URLs to third parties. The finding is a hygiene gap; no data flow is measured.
DPK-DAST-009.risk: URL and parameter leakage to other origins; LOW.

DPK-DAST-010.title: Concept: CSP without frame-ancestors
DPK-DAST-010.description: A Content-Security-Policy that omits frame-ancestors governs resource loading but leaves framing to other headers or to browser defaults, so the policy is incomplete for clickjacking defence. The check reads the directive list only.
DPK-DAST-010.applicability: Responses that send CSP without frame-ancestors.

DPK-SAST-001.title: Concept: Dynamic code evaluation
DPK-SAST-001.description: eval and its language equivalents compile a string at runtime. Once any part of that string is attacker-influenced the boundary between data and code disappears, which is why the safe form is a lookup table or an explicit parser rather than a sanitised string.
DPK-SAST-001.applicability: Any line that calls an eval-family sink; the rule does not prove that the argument is untrusted.
DPK-SAST-001.risk: Arbitrary code execution in the application process; MEDIUM per rule severity.

DPK-SAST-002.title: Concept: Raw HTML assignment sink
DPK-SAST-002.description: Assigning to innerHTML parses the string as markup, so text that reaches it becomes elements and handlers. A safe construction builds nodes and assigns textContent, keeping data out of the parser.
DPK-SAST-002.applicability: Browser-side assignments to raw HTML properties on a single line.
DPK-SAST-002.risk: Reflected or stored script execution in the victim browser; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-003.title: Concept: Shell invocation enabled
DPK-SAST-003.description: Passing shell=True to a subprocess call hands the command string to a shell, where metacharacters are syntax rather than data. An argument vector without the shell keeps the boundary intact.
DPK-SAST-003.applicability: Python subprocess calls that request a shell on the same line.
DPK-SAST-003.risk: Command execution under the service account; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-004.title: Concept: Broken hash primitive (MD5)
DPK-SAST-004.description: MD5 collisions are practical and its preimage resistance is below modern expectations, so it is unsuitable wherever a digest must stand for integrity or a password. The rule flags the call, not the purpose it serves.
DPK-SAST-004.applicability: Direct MD5 calls; qualified or aliased spellings may escape a lexical match.
DPK-SAST-004.risk: Integrity forgery or fast offline cracking; LOW per rule severity.

DPK-SAST-005.title: Concept: Native-object deserialization
DPK-SAST-005.description: pickle reconstructs arbitrary Python objects, and its opcodes can import and call code during load. Data from an untrusted source therefore becomes execution, and only a data-only format keeps the operation inert.
DPK-SAST-005.applicability: Python pickle load calls on a single line.
DPK-SAST-005.risk: Remote code execution when untrusted bytes are loaded; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-006.title: Concept: PHP shell functions
DPK-SAST-006.description: Functions such as system, exec, shell_exec and passthru run their argument through a shell. Escaping is context-sensitive and easy to get wrong, so the durable fix is an argument-vector API or a fixed command allowlist.
DPK-SAST-006.applicability: Direct calls to PHP shell functions.
DPK-SAST-006.risk: Command execution in the web process; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-007.title: Concept: Unbounded C string copy
DPK-SAST-007.description: strcpy and strcat write until a terminator without knowing the destination size, so input length decides whether adjacent memory is overwritten. Length-aware alternatives take the capacity as an explicit argument.
DPK-SAST-007.applicability: Direct calls to unbounded copy functions.
DPK-SAST-007.risk: Memory corruption and possible code execution; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-008.title: Concept: SQL assembled by concatenation
DPK-SAST-008.description: When a query is built by joining strings, the database parses the concatenated text as SQL and cannot tell a value from syntax. Parameter binding keeps the statement shape fixed and the value typed as data.
DPK-SAST-008.applicability: Query construction visible on one line; multi-line builders and ORM expressions are out of lexical scope.
DPK-SAST-008.risk: Data disclosure or modification across tenant boundaries; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-009.title: Concept: Document write sink
DPK-SAST-009.description: document.write injects its argument into the parsing stream, so markup is created at the insertion point. Rendering through DOM APIs with text nodes avoids re-entering the HTML parser.
DPK-SAST-009.applicability: Direct document.write calls in browser code.
DPK-SAST-009.risk: Script execution in the origin of the page; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-010.title: Concept: OS command passthrough
DPK-SAST-010.description: os.system passes its string to the platform shell, where spaces, semicolons and substitutions are interpreted. Composing the command with untrusted values therefore changes which commands run.
DPK-SAST-010.applicability: Direct os.system calls on one line.
DPK-SAST-010.risk: Command execution with service privileges; HIGH.

DPK-SAST-011.title: Concept: Unbounded input read
DPK-SAST-011.description: gets reads until a newline with no destination bound, so the input length controls the write. The function was removed from later C standards for this reason; fgets with a size is the bounded form.
DPK-SAST-011.applicability: Calls to gets in C sources.

DPK-SAST-012.title: Concept: YAML object construction
DPK-SAST-012.description: yaml.load with the default loader can construct arbitrary Python objects from tags, which is code execution during parsing. safe_load restricts the document to plain data types.
DPK-SAST-012.applicability: Direct yaml.load calls without an explicit safe loader on the same line.
DPK-SAST-012.risk: Code execution from a crafted document; HIGH.

DPK-SAST-013.title: Concept: Non-cryptographic randomness
DPK-SAST-013.description: Math.random is a fast seeded generator whose output can be predicted from observed values, so it is unsuitable for tokens, identifiers or keys. The cryptographic oracle is the platform crypto module.
DPK-SAST-013.applicability: Math.random calls where the surrounding purpose is not analysed.
DPK-SAST-013.risk: Token prediction and session forgery; LOW per rule severity, higher in auth flows.

DPK-SAST-014.title: Concept: Unhardened XML parser
DPK-SAST-014.description: A parser that resolves external entities will fetch or read whatever the document points at, turning XML input into file disclosure or server-side requests. Disabling DTD and external entity resolution removes the capability.
DPK-SAST-014.applicability: Parser construction visible on one line; hardening applied later in configuration is not seen.
DPK-SAST-014.risk: Local file read and outbound request forgery; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-015.title: Concept: Debug mode in application code
DPK-SAST-015.description: Debug modes trade safety for visibility: interactive error pages, verbose stack traces and sometimes an execution console. Shipping the flag in application code keeps that surface reachable in production.
DPK-SAST-015.applicability: Framework debug flags set in source rather than environment configuration.
DPK-SAST-015.risk: Information disclosure and, for some frameworks, code execution; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-016.title: Concept: Token decode without verified signature
DPK-SAST-016.description: A decode call that does not verify the signature returns attacker-controlled claims as if they were trusted. Verification must be an explicit, non-optional step with the expected algorithm pinned.
DPK-SAST-016.applicability: JWT decode calls whose verification options are not visible on the line.

DPK-SAST-017.title: Concept: Wildcard CORS origin
DPK-SAST-017.description: Allowing every origin lets any site read responses that the browser would otherwise fence off, which matters as soon as the response is authenticated or tenant-specific. An explicit allowlist restores the boundary.
DPK-SAST-017.applicability: CORS configuration assigning a wildcard origin.
DPK-SAST-017.risk: Cross-origin data theft from logged-in users; MEDIUM.

DPK-SAST-018.title: Concept: Public-read storage ACL
DPK-SAST-018.description: A public-read ACL makes each object readable by anyone with the URL, independent of application authorization. Bucket policies and signed access keep object retrieval under the application decision.
DPK-SAST-018.applicability: Storage ACL declarations in source or infrastructure code.
DPK-SAST-018.risk: Bulk data exposure through object enumeration; HIGH.

DPK-SAST-019.title: Concept: Peer verification disabled
DPK-SAST-019.description: verify=False accepts any certificate, so the client cannot distinguish the intended server from an interceptor. The setting is sometimes added to silence a local error and then survives into production.
DPK-SAST-019.applicability: HTTP client calls that pass an explicit verification-off flag.
DPK-SAST-019.risk: Credential and response interception by a network attacker; HIGH.

DPK-SAST-020.title: Concept: ECB block-cipher mode
DPK-SAST-020.description: ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks into identical ciphertext blocks, leaking structure and enabling block splicing. A mode with an unpredictable IV, such as CBC with a random IV or an AEAD, removes the pattern.
DPK-SAST-020.applicability: Cipher construction using an ECB mode constant.
DPK-SAST-020.risk: Plaintext structure disclosure and ciphertext manipulation; HIGH.

DPK-SAST-021.title: Concept: Internet-open network rule
DPK-SAST-021.description: A 0.0.0.0/0 ingress rule exposes the port to every address on the internet, so any missing authentication is reachable. Narrowing the source to the intended network is an infrastructure-level decision.
DPK-SAST-021.applicability: Security-group or firewall rules declaring an all-address source.
DPK-SAST-021.risk: Direct exposure of administrative or data services; HIGH.

DPK-SAST-022.title: Concept: Secret key embedded in source
DPK-SAST-022.description: A signing or encryption key committed with the code is readable by everyone who can read the repository and survives in history after removal. Keys belong in secret storage and should be rotated when exposed.
DPK-SAST-022.applicability: Assignments of secret-looking values to key-named variables.
DPK-SAST-022.risk: Session forgery or decryption wherever the key is trusted; HIGH.

DPK-SEC-001.title: Concept: Cloud access key identifier in source
DPK-SEC-001.description: An access key identifier names the principal that the paired secret authenticates. On its own it cannot sign requests, but committed beside its secret it turns a repository leak into account access, and it identifies the account to an attacker.
DPK-SEC-001.applicability: High-confidence identifier shapes in any text file; secret pairing is not evaluated.
DPK-SEC-001.risk: Account reconnaissance and, with the secret, full API access; MEDIUM.

DPK-SEC-002.title: Concept: Personal access token in source
DPK-SEC-002.description: A personal access token carries its owner scopes directly, so anyone who reads it acts as that user until revocation. Repository history and CI logs are common unintended distribution channels.
DPK-SEC-002.applicability: Token-shaped strings matching the documented prefix grammar.
DPK-SEC-002.risk: Repository and API access with the owner scopes; HIGH.

DPK-SEC-003.title: Concept: API key assigned in source
DPK-SEC-003.description: A generic API key has no self-describing prefix, so detection relies on assignment shape plus entropy rather than a vendor grammar. The finding says a credential-shaped literal is committed, not which service honours it.
DPK-SEC-003.applicability: Assignments of high-entropy values to key-named identifiers.
DPK-SEC-003.risk: Service abuse within the key quota or scope; MEDIUM.

DPK-SEC-004.title: Concept: Private key material committed
DPK-SEC-004.description: A PEM private-key header marks the start of an actual key, not a credential reference. Anyone with the file can impersonate the key owner, and rotation requires reissuing the certificate or key pair.
DPK-SEC-004.applicability: PEM private-key block headers in any file.
DPK-SEC-004.risk: Identity impersonation and traffic decryption; HIGH.

DPK-SEC-005.title: Concept: Workspace bot token in source
DPK-SEC-005.description: A workspace bot token authenticates as the installed app across its channels, so a leak grants posting and data access beyond one conversation. Tokens are revocable per installation.
DPK-SEC-005.applicability: Token-shaped strings matching the documented workspace prefix grammar.
DPK-SEC-005.risk: Message posting and workspace data access; HIGH.

DPK-SEC-006.title: Concept: Cloud secret access key in source
DPK-SEC-006.description: The secret half of a cloud key pair signs requests, so it is directly usable when committed. Unlike the identifier it grants immediate API access until deactivated.
DPK-SEC-006.applicability: High-entropy values assigned to secret-key-named identifiers.
DPK-SEC-006.risk: Full API access under the key principal; HIGH.

DPK-SEC-007.title: Concept: Password literal in source
DPK-SEC-007.description: A password written into configuration or code authenticates to whatever consumes it and is shared by every deployment of that revision. The fix is externalised secret storage plus rotation of the exposed credential.
DPK-SEC-007.applicability: Password-named assignments with a non-placeholder literal.
DPK-SEC-007.risk: Authentication bypass where the credential is reused; HIGH.

DPK-SEC-008.title: Concept: Fine-grained token in source
DPK-SEC-008.description: A fine-grained token scopes access to named repositories and permissions, which limits but does not remove the impact of a leak. It remains valid until expiry or revocation.
DPK-SEC-008.applicability: Token-shaped strings matching the fine-grained prefix grammar.
DPK-SEC-008.risk: Scoped repository access for the token lifetime; HIGH.
